newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese pound continues rise against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese pound continues rise against dollar.

text.p: The Lebanese pound continued its rise against the U.S. dollar in the week ended Friday on a quiet market despite falling interest rates, dealers said.

The Bank of Lebanon lowered its bid-offer intervention band to 1,545-1,554.5 pounds per dollar from 1,545.5-1,555 and the dollar continued to trade at the bottom of the band throughout the week, dealers said.

"It is still the same trend, there is dollar offer and pound demand orders because investors see the trend of the Lebanese pound interest rates decreasing," Talal Abou Zaki, manager of forex and money market for Bank of Beirut and The Arab Countries, told Reuters.

Yields on Lebanese pound-denominated treasury bills continued to fall during the week. They now stand at 14.08 percent for three month bills, 15.56 percent for six months, 15.84 percent for 12 months and 17.14 percent for 24-month bills.

Trade on the foreign exchange market was restricted to a very tight range of 10-15 and maximum 20 piastres at the bid end of the central bank's intervention band, Abou Zaki said. All the offers of dollars were taken up by commercial banks, he added.
